0) — this end-of-run pass is the whole filing (file-and-defer).

1. **Collect.** Glob `.faff/runs/<run-id>/*/discovered-scope.json` (each built issue's file; absent when it found nothing). Every built issue contributes regardless of its terminal outcome — a `shipped`, `pr-open`, or `parked` issue can all carry discovered scope. **Also read the orchestrator-lane file `.faff/runs/<run-id>/orchestrator/discovered-scope.json`** (defects the orchestrator itself hit; see _Orchestrator-lane capture_ below). Orchestrator entries flow through steps 2–7 exactly as implementor entries do, with one difference recorded at step 6: their mandate is the **run's dispatch container**, and — no per-issue mandate issue exists for them — their surface-only target is the run summary + `/faff-wtf` §4 only (no per-issue comment).
2. **Containment check (runs before the appetite gate; this is chokepoint #1).** This step is an autonomous-by-construction create path, so each `concrete` item passes `autonomous_file_check` (see _Containment at the filing chokepoint_ below) **before** the gate. The **mandate is the `<ISSUE>` dir the item came from** — the built issue beep-boop was dispatched from the human-admitted queue (for orchestrator-lane entries, the run's dispatch container). Fetch the intended parent's ancestry **fresh** and call `faff contain … --record <run-id> --phase run` (see the procedure below). `outward` (or an item graft already tagged `containment: outward-new-root`) → skip steps 3–4, jump to step 6 (surface-only) — **unless** the self-hosting-intake lane reclassifies it `outward-self-intake` inside the procedure, in which case it rejoins the appetite gate (steps 3–5). `contained` → fall through to the appetite gate. `vague` items skip the check (they are never filed regardless).
3. **Gate per item:**
   - `vague` items → never filed. Aggregate for the run summary + the next `/faff-wtf` morning brief only.
   - `concrete` + `contained` items (and `concrete` + `outward-self-intake` items — the self-intake lane, which reaches this gate having already passed the same-team structural check inside the procedure) → **appetite-gated** (gateway → **Appetite for destruction**, _Execution-discovered auto-create_ row): `low` surfaces only; `medium` files only with an opinionated methodology; `high` (default) files every concrete item; `full` always files. An `outward-new-root` item is **never** filed at any level including `full` (the hard floor) — it was already routed to step 6.
4. **Dedup before creating.** Match each item's title/surface + relationship target against existing open tickets (a build often "discovers" a downstream the spec already named and tidy already filled; a self-intake defect is deduped against the same open-ticket set as any other item). Skip duplicates; count them.
5. **File** each surviving item per the chain-gap recipe (see `/faff-tidy` → _Chain gaps_ — do not restate it): status `Backlog`, the recorded relationship link to the originating issue, and a "discovered during build of SHF-XX" provenance line in the description. **Stamp `initiated: autonomous`** on the create — `faff intake-record <new-issue> --via jot --initiated autonomous` (the marker is the autonomous-filing audit trail). **When the item's `priority` is present (not `absent`):** set the tracker priority and post the fixed-shape reason comment per `/faff-graft` → _Discovered scope_ → **The priority-reason comment** (do not restate it), attributed to `/faff-beep-boop`, in the same create call that sets status/relationship/provenance. `entry.priority` was already computed at capture time (graft Steps 7/9/10, or the orchestrator capture below) — this step reads it, it never recomputes it. An item whose `priority` is `absent` (vague, or a legacy entry predating this field) files exactly as before — no tracker priority, no comment. **Self-intake exception:** an item classified `outward-self-intake` files to the **self-intake lane** instead — status `Backlog`, no `faff-automate`; it is a defect record rather than a chain gap, and the `outward-self-intake` containment classification recorded in the run's discovered-scope entry (not on the ticket) is what says so; same `--via jot --initiated autonomous` stamp; relationship link only when the entry names one; the same priority/comment handling applies when the entry carries one. On an opted-out L3 run (file-and-defer timing) the next run's tidy + prep pass picks them up — depth grows one layer per run; under the convergence loop (the default; forced at L4 — filed at step 8.0) the *same* run's wave re-entry picks up the eligible ones — depth grows many layers per run, bounded by `faff run-done`.
6. **Outward-new-root (surface-only, never filed).** For each `outward` item: keep/record its `DiscoveredScopeEntry { containment: "outward-new-root" }`, **create nothing**, surface it in the run summary's discovered-scope section so `/faff-wtf` §4 shows it, **and post a comment on the mandate issue** (the `<ISSUE>` it came from — an already-sanctioned surface, so the comment is in-lane, not scope expansion). **Orchestrator-lane entries have no mandate issue** — skip the per-issue comment; the run summary + `/faff-wtf` §4 are their sanctioned surfaces. Do **not** park the build. The human creating the root later via `/faff-jot` (→ `initiated: interactive`) is the approval.
7. **Record** the filed count to the ledger's informational `discovered_scope_filed` field (see Run ledger) and log per-item (id, source issue, relationship, containment verdict, gate decision) under `.faff/runs/<run-id>/discovered-scope-filed.md`.

Filed tickets are **new work, not admitted issues** — they sit outside runcheck's `admitted − outcomes` invariant and never affect run completeness.
